text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 11 in history.
1503 - Parmigianino, Italian painter and one of the first to rebel against High Renaissance art, born as Girolamo Francesco Maria Mazzola.
1814 - Joachim Murat, King of Naples, ended his association with Napoleon and entered into an alliance with the Austrians.
1815 - Sir John Macdonald, Canada's first prime minister from 1867-73, born.
1843 - Francis Scott Key, U.S. lawyer and poet who wrote the words to the national anthem "The Star Spangled Banner", died.
1902 - French organist and composer, Maurice Durufle, born. Noted for his "Trois Danses" and the much-performed "Requiem".
1904 - The Herero people of South West Africa began an uprising against the German colonisers.
1907 - Pierre Mendes-France was born. Became French prime minister in 1954 and oversaw the end of French involvement in the war in Indochina, but was defeated in 1955 over the Algerian rebellion.
1911 - Zenko Suzuki, Japanese prime minister 1980-83, born.
1922 - A 14-year-old-boy, Canadian Leonard Thompson, became the first person to have his diabetes successfully treated with insulin.
1928 - Thomas Hardy, English novelist and poet, died. Noted for his books "The Mayor of Casterbridge" and "Tess of the d'Urbervilles".
1946 - Albania became a people's republic after King Zog was overthrown.
1962 - Over 3,000 people were killed in a landslide in Huascaran, Peru.
1970 - Biafran leader General Ojukwu flew into exile, after Nigerian troops captured the capital Owerri the previous day.
1972 - Padraic Colum, Irish playwright and poet, died.
1974 - The first sextuplets to survive were born to Sue Rosenkowitz in Cape Town, South Africa.
1981 - Three-man British team led by Sir Ranulph Fiennes completed the longest and fastest crossing of Antarctica, reaching Scott base after 75 days and 2,500 miles.
1991 - Soviet troops stormed strategic buildings in the Lithuanian capital Vilnius to block a bid for independence.
1992 - Algeria's President Chadli announced his resignation amid a political crisis following gains by the Islamic Salvation Front in the first round of general elections.
1993 - Richard Branson won huge libel damages and an apology from British Airways over an alleged dirty tricks campaign against his Virgin Atlantic Airways.
1994 - The Irish government announced the end of a 20-year broadcasting ban on the IRA and its political arm Sinn Fein.
1996 - Italian Prime Minister Lamberto Dini announced his resignation saying his government of unelected technocrats had reached its end.
1996 - Ryutaro Hashimoto took over as Japan's prime minister.
